questions.q: Which license is required to use the full set of Microsoft Entra ID Protection capabilities, including risk-based Conditional Access policies and full risk reports?
options: Microsoft Entra ID Free
Microsoft Entra ID P1
Microsoft Entra ID P2
Microsoft Entra ID Governance
questions.explanation: ID Protection needs Entra ID P2 (or the Microsoft Entra Suite). Free and P1 tenants get only limited risk data and nonpremium detections.

questions.q: An administrator with only Entra ID P1 licenses sees a detection titled Additional risk detected with no further details. What does this mean?
options: A premium detection fired, but its details are visible only with Entra ID P2
The detection was a false positive that ID Protection dismissed automatically after reviewing it
An administrator generated the detection manually
The detection came from Defender for Cloud Apps and needs that license
questions.explanation: Premium detections are labeled Additional risk detected for tenants without P2, so you know something risky happened but can't see the detection type or details.

questions.q: Which of these detections is available in tenants that don't have Entra ID P2 (a nonpremium detection)?
options: Atypical travel between two geographically distant locations
Unfamiliar sign-in properties
Password spray
Leaked credentials
questions.explanation: Leaked credentials, Anonymous IP address, Microsoft Entra threat intelligence and Admin confirmed user compromised are nonpremium. The others require P2.

questions.q: Security analysts must view all ID Protection reports and dismiss user risk or confirm compromise, but must not configure policies or reset passwords. Which role is the least-privileged fit?
options: Security Reader
Security Operator
Global Reader with read-only directory access
Security Administrator
questions.explanation: Security Operator can view reports and dismiss user risk, confirm safe sign-ins and confirm compromise. Security Reader and Global Reader are read-only, and Security Administrator can also configure policies.

questions.q: Which role is the least-privileged option for creating Conditional Access policies that use user risk or sign-in risk as a condition?
options: Security Operator assigned at tenant scope
Security Reader
Conditional Access Administrator
Global Reader with read-only directory access
questions.explanation: Conditional Access Administrators can create policies that factor in user or sign-in risk. The other roles can't create or edit Conditional Access policies.

questions.q: A Security Administrator is investigating a risky user and tries to reset the user's password from the Risky users report, but can't. Which role provides that ability?
options: User Administrator
Security Operator assigned at tenant scope
Reports Reader
Global Reader with read-only directory access
questions.explanation: Security Administrators have full access to ID Protection but can't reset passwords. A User Administrator is needed to reset a user's password.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes user risk in Microsoft Entra ID Protection?
options: It represents the probability that a specific authentication request wasn't made by the account owner
It counts the failed sign-ins recorded in the last 24 hours
It represents how many devices a user has registered
It represents the probability that an identity or account is compromised
questions.explanation: User risk is about the likelihood that the account is compromised and persists until remediated. Sign-in risk is about a single authentication request.

questions.q: How long do low-risk detections and low-risk users persist in ID Protection?
options: 30 days
About six months, after which they age out automatically
Until an administrator dismisses or remediates them, as with medium and high risk
90 days
questions.explanation: Low-level detections and users age out after six months to keep investigations focused. Medium and high risk persist until remediated or dismissed.

questions.q: How long can it take for an offline-calculated risk detection to appear in the reports?
options: Up to 48 hours
5 to 10 minutes
Up to 7 days
It is shown immediately
questions.explanation: Real-time detections surface in 5 to 10 minutes, while offline detections can take up to 48 hours. Risk levels can change after sign-in because some detections are calculated offline.

questions.q: A tenant with only Entra ID Free licenses needs a real-time detection of sign-ins from anonymous IP addresses such as Tor. Which detection provides this?
options: Activity from anonymous IP address
Malicious IP address
Anonymous IP address
Verified threat actor IP
questions.explanation: Anonymous IP address is calculated in real time and is a nonpremium detection. Activity from anonymous IP address comes from Defender for Cloud Apps, is offline and premium.

questions.q: A hybrid tenant receives a leaked credentials detection for a synchronized user. What is required for a cloud-based password reset to remediate the on-premises password?
options: Pass-through authentication must be enabled on at least three agents
AD FS must be deployed
Seamless SSO must be enabled
Password hash synchronization must be enabled
questions.explanation: A secure password reset in Entra ID remediates leaked credentials for on-premises passwords only if password hash synchronization is enabled.

questions.q: Which statement about the password spray detection is correct?
options: It triggers on every burst of failed sign-ins against a user from a single IP address
It triggers only when an attacker successfully validates a user's password, not on failed attempts
It is a nonpremium detection available with Free
It is calculated only offline
questions.explanation: Unsuccessful spray attempts don't generate a detection. When it fires, Microsoft observed a spray attack and a successful credential validation against a user in your tenant.

questions.q: A company wants to use the Impossible travel detection. In addition to Entra ID P2, which license is required?
options: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, as a standalone license or through Microsoft 365 E5 with EMS E5
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Plan 2 on each managed device
Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management
Microsoft Entra ID Governance
questions.explanation: Impossible travel is discovered using Defender for Cloud Apps and calculated offline. Atypical travel is a separate real-time detection that needs only P2.

questions.q: A user account was created yesterday, and a sign-in from an unusual browser and country didn't produce an unfamiliar sign-in properties detection. What is the likely reason?
options: The detection works only for interactive sign-ins and ignores non-interactive ones entirely
The detection requires Defender for Cloud Apps
New users are in a learning mode, with a minimum of five days, during which the detection is off
The detection is offline and takes 30 days to appear
questions.explanation: Newly created users are in a learning period that lasts at least five days while ID Protection learns their sign-in patterns. A user can re-enter learning mode after long inactivity.

questions.q: Which detection indicates that the issuer of a SAML token might be compromised?
options: Anomalous token
Token issuer anomaly
Suspicious browser
Anomalous user activity
questions.explanation: Token issuer anomaly flags SAML token issuers whose claims are unusual or match known attacker patterns. Anomalous token flags abnormal token characteristics such as lifetime or replay from unfamiliar locations.

questions.q: Users deny unexpected MFA prompts and report them as suspicious, yet no User reported suspicious activity detections appear in ID Protection. What is the likely cause?
options: The detection requires Entra ID Governance
The detections appear only after a 90-day learning period for the tenant
Users must hold the Security Reader role
The Report suspicious activity setting isn't turned on
questions.explanation: The user reported suspicious activity detection works only when Report suspicious activity is turned on in the MFA settings. It is an offline, premium detection.

questions.q: Which detection compares properties such as ASN, browser, device and GPS proximity between the requesting and approving devices to flag likely MFA phishing?
options: Suspicious MFA authentication approval
Atypical travel between two geographically distant locations
Suspicious browser
Anomalous user activity
questions.explanation: Suspicious MFA authentication approval is a real-time premium detection that uses Authenticator telemetry for password plus MFA sign-ins and flags the sign-in as high risk.

questions.q: Which user risk detection fires only in organizations that deploy Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and moves the user to high risk?
options: Suspicious API traffic against Microsoft Graph and directory enumeration
Anomalous user activity
Possible attempt to access Primary Refresh Token (PRT)
Leaked credentials
questions.explanation: The PRT detection uses Defender for Endpoint information and raises users to high risk. Leaked credentials is a Microsoft-sourced nonpremium detection.

questions.q: Your tenant still uses legacy user risk and sign-in risk policies configured inside ID Protection. What should you do?
options: Nothing; the legacy ID Protection policies remain the recommended approach for risk-based access
Replace them with security defaults
Move them to the Authentication methods policy
Migrate them to risk-based Conditional Access policies, since Microsoft scheduled the legacy policies for retirement on October 1, 2026
questions.explanation: Risk policies are configured in Conditional Access, which offers more conditions and session controls. Create equivalent policies in report-only mode first, then enforce them and disable the legacy ones.

questions.q: You are creating a sign-in risk policy in Conditional Access. Which configuration matches Microsoft's recommendation?
options: Sign-in risk of Low and above, requiring a password change and terms of use acceptance
Sign-in risk of Medium and High, requiring MFA (or an MFA authentication strength)
Sign-in risk of High only, requiring terms of use
Sign-in risk of None, requiring a compliant device
questions.explanation: Sign-in risk calls for proving identity with MFA. Requiring controls at Low risk adds more friction and interruptions than Medium or High.

questions.q: You are creating a user risk policy in Conditional Access. Which configuration matches Microsoft's recommendation?
options: User risk of High, requiring MFA and a secure password change, with sign-in frequency set to Every time
User risk of Low, requiring MFA only and a sign-in frequency of 90 days
User risk of Medium, requiring terms of use
User risk of High, requiring an approved client app
questions.explanation: A compromised account needs a secure password change, which requires MFA first. Sign-in frequency Every time forces reauthentication until the risk is remediated.

questions.q: A user is assigned to three Conditional Access risk policies: one blocks access, one requires risk remediation, and one requires a password change. Which result applies?
options: Require password change applies, because it is the most specific control and is evaluated last
Require risk remediation applies, because it is evaluated first
Access is blocked, because Block overrides Require risk remediation, which overrides Require password change
The most recently created policy applies
questions.explanation: Block takes precedence over everything, and Require risk remediation overrides Require password change. Assign each user to only one risk policy at a time to avoid conflicts.

questions.q: Many users sign in without passwords, so Require password change isn't meaningful for them. Which grant control lets ID Protection manage the right remediation flow for all authentication methods?
options: Require password change
Require risk remediation
Require authentication strength
Require terms of use
questions.explanation: Require risk remediation lets ID Protection choose the appropriate remediation, which works for passwordless users as well as password-based users.

questions.q: Hybrid users synchronized with only password hash synchronization must be able to remediate user risk by changing their on-premises password. Which setting should you enable?
options: Seamless single sign-on for hybrid joined devices
Password protection in audit mode
Federation for the domain
Allow on-premises password change to reset user risk
questions.explanation: With PHS only, enabling Allow on-premises password change to reset user risk lets a password change from a hybrid joined Windows device remediate risk. Alternatively, use SSPR with password writeback.

questions.q: A high-risk user changes their password on the My Account page by entering the old password. Is the user risk remediated?
options: No; only a secure password change completed in the risk remediation flow remediates user risk
Yes; any password change, including one that uses the old password, clears user risk
Yes, but only for cloud-only users
No; only an administrator can ever remediate user risk
questions.explanation: A password change outside the risky user remediation flow doesn't meet the secure password change requirement. The user must authenticate with MFA and then change the password through the flow.

questions.q: Which prerequisite must be in place for users to self-remediate risk through risk-based policies?
options: Users must be members of the Security Reader role in the tenant
Users must be on hybrid joined devices
Users must have previously registered for MFA and SSPR
Users must have enabled passwordless sign-in
questions.explanation: Self-remediation relies on the user completing MFA or a secure password change, so they must have registered the required methods ahead of time. Otherwise an administrator must remediate.

questions.q: After an investigation, an administrator determines that a flagged sign-in was legitimate and wants similar sign-ins to stop being treated as risky. Which action should the administrator choose?
options: Dismiss sign-in risk
Confirm sign-in safe
Confirm sign-in compromised
Confirm user compromised
questions.explanation: Confirm sign-in safe marks a false positive and teaches ID Protection that similar sign-ins shouldn't be risky. Dismiss is for a benign true positive.

questions.q: An administrator dismisses a user's risk after investigating. What is the effect?
options: The user's password is reset automatically
The user's refresh tokens are revoked and all sessions end immediately
The user is blocked until MFA is registered
The risk state becomes Dismissed, and the user's existing password isn't changed
questions.explanation: Dismissing user risk changes the state from At risk to Dismissed but doesn't touch the password, so the identity isn't necessarily back in a safe state.

questions.q: An administrator selects Confirm user compromised for a user. What is the effect?
options: The user's risk is raised to High, and an Admin confirmed user compromised detection is recorded
The user's account is deleted
The user's risk is dismissed and the detection is archived for 30 days
The user's password is reset to a temporary value
questions.explanation: Confirming compromise marks the user as a true positive, which raises the user to high risk and records the Admin confirmed user compromised detection. Remediation then still needs a secure password reset.

questions.q: Why should organizations deploy risk-based policies that let users self-remediate sign-in risk?
options: Sign-in risk is ignored by user risk calculations, so remediation is optional
Sign-in risks that aren't remediated affect the user's risk level
Self-remediation is mandatory in Free tenants
Risk-based policies remove the need to register for MFA
questions.explanation: Unremediated sign-in risk feeds into user risk. A sign-in risk policy that requires MFA lets users prove identity so their user risk isn't raised.

questions.q: Which risk level triggers the Users at risk detected email by default?
options: Low
Medium
High
Any risk detection
questions.explanation: By default the alert is configured for high risk, and you can lower the level. The email goes to Global Administrators, Security Administrators and Security Readers by default.

questions.q: What does the ID Protection weekly digest email contain?
options: A list of every user's MFA registration status and authentication methods
Only risky users that stayed unremediated for 7 days
A count of failed password resets
A summary of new risky users and new real-time risky sign-ins, with links to the reports
questions.explanation: The weekly digest summarizes newly detected risky users and risky sign-ins (in real time) and links to the related reports. You can turn it on or off and choose its recipients.

questions.q: A SOC wants ID Protection risk data in Microsoft Sentinel. What should you configure?
options: Microsoft Entra diagnostic settings that stream risky users and user risk events
Weekly digest forwarding to a mail-enabled security group that feeds Sentinel
A Conditional Access report-only policy
Password protection audit logs
questions.explanation: Diagnostic settings can send risky user and risk event logs to Log Analytics, Sentinel, a storage account or an event hub for correlation.

questions.q: A guest from a partner tenant is blocked by a user risk policy in your tenant, and the guest's home tenant has SSPR disabled. How can the risk be resolved?
options: Your Security Administrator can reset the password of the guest's home account
The guest can self-remediate with a Temporary Access Pass from your tenant
The guest's home organization IT staff must dismiss the risk or reset the guest's password
Remove the guest's licenses from your tenant
questions.explanation: If the guest has no SSPR in their home directory, they must contact their own organization's IT staff to manually dismiss the risk or reset the password.

questions.q: Which license is required to use the risky workload identities report and workload identity detections?
options: Entra ID P1
Workload Identities Premium
Entra ID Governance
Microsoft Defender for Identity
questions.explanation: Full workload identity risk details and risk-based access controls need Workload Identities Premium. Without it you still receive detections with limited reporting.

questions.q: Which ID Protection report lists each individual detection, including its type, whether it was real-time or offline, and its risk level?
options: Risky users report
Risky sign-ins report
Authentication methods activity report
Risk detections report
questions.explanation: The Risk detections report lists every detection with its details. Risky users and risky sign-ins summarize the accounts and sign-ins that are at risk.

questions.q: Which user risk detection baselines normal administrative behavior and flags suspicious changes to the directory?
options: Anomalous user activity
Suspicious API traffic against Microsoft Graph and directory enumeration
Token issuer anomaly
New country
questions.explanation: Anomalous user activity is an offline premium detection that flags unusual administrative actions against the administrator or the changed object.

questions.q: What data is available in the Risky users report for tenants with only Entra ID Free or P1?
options: No access at all
Limited data about risky users; full access requires Entra ID P2
Full access, because the report is a Free feature
Full access to risky users, but without any risk history or remediation actions
questions.explanation: Free and P1 tenants get limited user risk information, while P2 gives full access to risky user data, history and remediation actions.

questions.q: A risky sign-in shows risk state Dismissed with the detail Microsoft Entra ID Protection assessed sign-in safe. What happened?
options: An administrator confirmed the sign-in as compromised and ID Protection blocked the user
The user completed MFA
An administrator reset the user's password
System-based remediation automatically dismissed the risk after assessing the sign-in as safe
questions.explanation: ID Protection can automatically dismiss risk it later determines to be benign, reducing noise. User self-remediation shows as Remediated, not Dismissed.

questions.q: A junior analyst must view all ID Protection reports but must not be able to dismiss risk, confirm compromise or change settings. Which role fits?
options: Security Operator assigned at tenant scope
Security Administrator
Security Reader
User Administrator
questions.explanation: Security Reader is read-only for ID Protection. Security Operator can also dismiss risk and confirm compromise, and Security Administrator can change settings.
